style: UK garage 2-step, 132 bpm, skippy swung sixteenth hats, broken kick, rubbery sub bass, chopped vocal stab, heard muffled through a club door at 2am, low-pass filtered, street air. Spoken word, not rapped, not sung: a cocky young South London MC voice, drunk, giddy, too loud. Mid-track the groove stutters, gates, beat-repeats and doubles into glitched copies of itself, then a hard stop into total silence. Second voice: a very deep, slow bass-baritone man, dry, close-mic, unhurried, no reverb, nothing under him. Ending: one low sub boom and a single taxi horn pitched to the key, cinematic, rings out. Short sound-design cue, speech-led.
exclude: singing, melody vocals, rap flow, autotune, choir, female vocals, four-on-the-floor house, EDM drop, long intro, fade-in, outro jam, repeated lyrics, crowd cheering
lyrics:
[Intro: 2-step groove through a club door, muffled]

[Spoken: cocky drunk young MC, half-shouting over the beat]
There's infinite versions of me. One of them gets home fine.

[Break: beat stutters, chops and doubles into glitch copies]

[Hard stop: dead silence, no music]

[Spoken: very deep slow bass-baritone man, dry and close]
There's only one.

[Sub boom, one taxi horn in key, ring out]

[End]
title: infinite yous r1-garage-pulse-cut-dead
